content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm working with a test system that uses a [product_name] controller. My tests run for durations between 1-30 days, but I've encountered a storage limitation—only 20,000 data entries can be saved to the memory card. I'd like to record data every 5 seconds for 30 days, which would amount to roughly 520,000 entries, and ideally log this data directly to a computer over the network. Best regards, [user_name]

When using the [product_name] [article_no], there are three main ways to log data: • You can use a custom DataLog without an SD card, but you’re limited to 512 bytes of logged data. Once the limit is reached, the oldest entry is removed to make room for new ones (FIFO method). • With a DataLog on an SD card, you can create up to 50 log files, each containing 20,000 entries. After reaching the file limit, a new log file is started. • With the [product_name] Access Tool, data is logged directly to a PC using Excel at a fixed interval of one second, which cannot be changed. If these approaches don’t meet your needs, you may need to find third-party apps or software that offer more customizable options or consider programming your own solution.

Hi, you can find more information at [url]. On the right side, look for 'more about [product_name]' and select the 'Update, Demo, ...' section. Scroll down to locate the [product_name] Access Tool, which is free to download. Once downloaded and unzipped, check the instructions to install and use it. The Access Tool is a Microsoft Excel add-in, allowing you to read data from [product_name] directly into an Excel CSV file. To log your data, use the instruction '=LOGOVAR L' instead of '=LOGOVAR.' The 'L' stands for logging. The tool records data every second as long as the connection to [product_name] is active. Alternatively, you can use the I/O Status tool to transfer I/O status and record all standard I/O data to a CSV file, provided the status window is open. Note, however, that VM memory and parameters can't be recorded using this method. Hope this helps.

Hello [user_name], Does this solution only work with Microsoft Excel, and does Excel need to stay open during the entire logging period? Is it possible to use OpenOffice or LibreOffice for similar functionality? Is there any option available for native Linux or Mac users? Kind regards, [user_name]
Please refer to the attached PDF document, page 5. Download link for the Access Tool: [url]

analysis.insight_summary: Users are facing limits with the storage capacity of both the internal memory and SD card when using [product_name] modules for long-term, high-frequency data logging. They want to log larger volumes of data directly to networked computers to bypass hardware restrictions. Official software like the [product_name] Access Tool relies on Microsoft Excel and offers little flexibility, particularly for users who prefer different operating systems or office suites, revealing a need for more adaptable and cross-platform logging solutions.
analysis.user_expectations: Users seek the ability to continuously log large amounts of data from [product_name] modules directly to network computers at custom intervals, without being constrained by SD card storage capacity or restricted to specific office software.
